questions.q_en: If a + b = √6 and a - b = √2; then what is the value of ab(a2 + b2)?
questions.solution_en:
As we know that, 4ab = (a + b)2 - (a - b)2

=>4ab = 6 - 2 = 4

=>ab = 1

Also; a2 + b2 = (a + b)2 - 2ab

=> a2 + b2 = 6 - 2 = 4

Hence required value = ab (a2 + b2) = 1 X 4 = 4

questions.q_en: If the number of even factors and odd factors of 440 is X and Y, then find the value of Y/X.
questions.solution_en:
440 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 5 x 11 = 23 x 51 x 111

Number of odd factors (leave the 2's) = (1 + 1) x (1 + 1) = 4 = X

Number of even factors = number of 2's x (1 + 1) x (1 + 1) = 12 = Y

Therefore,

Y/X = 12/4 = 3

questions.q_en: Saket has his final year exam at XYZ Engineering College. He left his home and travelled at a certain speed so that he would reach the college on time. After travelling half the distance, he realised that he left his admit card at home. He turned back immediately and increased his speed by 50% and reached his home. As compared to his original speed, by what percent should Saket increase his speed so that he still reaches the college on time?
questions.solution_en: Suppose the distance between home and college is 12 km and the speed is 2 kmph. It would take 6 hrs to reach college. When he reaches half way, he has already spent 3 hours. He turns back at a speed of 3 kmph and takes 6/3 = 2 hours to reach home. Now, he has only 1 hour to reach college. So the speed must be 12 kmph. Thus the increase in speed is (12-2)/2 X 100 = 500%.

questions.q_en: Ankit bought a book at 15% discount and a copy at 10% discount on the respective marked price. If the selling price of book and copy for Ankit is Rs.680 and Rs.1080 respectively, then what is the total discount percent received by Ankit?
questions.solution_en:
Marked price of book = 680 * (100/85) = Rs.800

Marked price of copy = 1080 * (100/90) = Rs.1200

Total marked price of book and copy together = 800 + 1200 = Rs.2000

Total selling price of book and copy together = 680 + 1080 = Rs.1760

Total discount amount = 2000 - 1760 = Rs.240

Required discount percent = (240/2000) * 100

= 12%

A bowler gives 13.6 runs per wicket. He gives 50 runs and takes 5 wickets in a match there by improving his average runs per wicket by (1/68)th times its earlier average. How many wickets had been taken by him till the last match.
questions.solution_en:
"

We know that, a bowler  improves his average by giving lesser runs per wicket. 

Here, improved average = 13.6 – (1/68) × 13.6 = 13.4

Let before the last match the bowler has taken x wicket

So, According to the question,

13.6 × x + 50 = (13.4) × (x + 5) 

  13.6x + 50 = 13.4x + 67

   0.2x = 17

   x = 85 

So, total wickets till last match = 85 + 5 = 90 

"

questions.q_en: Three taps P, Q and R alone can empty a tank in 8 hours, 4 hours, and 2 hours, respectively. When the tank is full, all three taps P, Q and R are opened one by one in the same order, but after an equal interval of 0.5 hour. In approximately how much time will the tank be empty?
questions.solution_en:
Part emptied by tap P in 1 hour = 1/8

Part emptied by tap Q in 1 hour = 1/4

Part emptied by tap R in 1 hour = 1/2

Let the time in which the tank is emptied be 'x' hours

Tap P was open for = x hours

Tap Q was open for = (x - 0.5) hours

Tap R was open for = (x - 1) hours

Now, part emptied by tank in x hours = 1

=> x/8 + (x - 0.5)/4 + (x - 1)/2 = 1

=> x/8 + (2x - 1)/8 + (4x - 4)/8 = 1

=> x + 2x - 1 + 4x - 4 = 8

=> 7x = 13

=> x = 13/7 hours ≅ 1 hour 51 min.

So, the tank will be empty in approximately 1 hour 51 min

questions.q_en: A State Transport bus covers a certain distance at an average speed of 75 kmph without stopping it. But with stoppages, it covers the same distance at an average speed of 50 kmph. Calculate for how many minutes per hour on average bus stops during its journey?
questions.solution_en:
A bus travelling at 75 kmph covers 75/60 i.e. 1.25 km per minute.

Now time to cover 50km by 1.25km per minute will be 40 minutes.

Therefore, at an average speed of 50kmph, the bus stops for 20 minutes on average every hour.

questions.q_en: The LCM of two numbers is 15 times their HCF. One number is the only cube between 100 and 200. The other number is 60% of the first number. Find the product of the digits of LCM.
questions.solution_en:
Let HCF = X then LCM = 15X

One number is the only cube between 100 and 200, which is 125.

Therefore, one number is 125.

Second number = 125 * 60/100 = 75

Now,

75 * 125 = X * 15X

X2 = 625

X = 25

Therefore,

LCM = 15 * 25 = 375

Required product = 3 * 7 * 5 = 105.

questions.q_en: Find the total amount of debt that will be discharged by 5 equal installments of Rs.200 each, if the debt is due in 5 years at 5% per annum simple interest.
questions.solution_en:
Assuming installments are made at the end of each year, each installment accrues simple interest up to the 5th year.

Payment at end of Year 1: 200 X (1 + 0.05 X 4) = 200 X 1.20 = 240

Payment at end of Year 2: 200 X (1 + 0.05 X 3) = 200 X 1.15 = 230

Payment at end of Year 3: 200 X (1 + 0.05 X 2) = 200 X 1.10 = 220

Payment at end of Year 4: 200 X (1 + 0.05 X 1) = 200 X 1.05 = 210

Payment at end of Year 5: 200 X (1 + 0.05 X 0) = 200

Total amount = 240 + 230 + 220 + 210 + 200 = 1100

questions.q_en: Two inlet pipes, P1 and P2, can fill a cistern in 20 hours and 30 hours, respectively. They were opened at the same time, but pipe P1 had to be closed 5 hours before the cistern was full. How many hours in total did it take for the two pipes to fill the cistern?
questions.solution_en:
Capacity of the cistern = LCM of 20 & 30 = 60 unit

Efficiency of pipe P1 = 60/20 = 3 units/hours

Efficiency of pipe P2 = 60/30 = 2 units/hours

Let the total time taken be 't' hours

According to question,

3(t - 5) + 2t = 60

3t - 15 + 2t = 60

5t = 75

t = 15 hours
